title: OTel exporter stabilization and dynamic metrics pruning
creator: Ava Chen
description: Reduce CPU and allocation overhead from the current tracing/metrics ingestion path by upgrading OpenTelemetry SDKs, moving to a more robust exporter configuration (gRPC + collector), and introducing dynamic metric pruning and low-cardinality wrappers. This ticket addresses production incidents where the observability pipeline amplified tail latency under bursty workloads and reduced node headroom due to high metric churn and blocking exporter IO.
background: Over the last 6 months we've observed several capacity incidents where telemetry fans out to many unique metric labels (high cardinality), causing metric store write amplification and excessive processing in our exporter goroutines. The existing custom async exporter has fragile backpressure behavior and non-optimal batching defaults. We also still carry an older OpenTelemetry SDK pinned behind several local shims that produce extra allocations and duplicate attributes. This manifests as: 1) increased p90/p99 request latencies on runtime hosts when telemetry spikes, 2) observable CPU burn in telemetry workers, 3) intermittent dropped traces during bursty import windows.
goals: Upgrade OpenTelemetry SDK and exporter deps to the supported 1.x stable line to pick up performance and bug fixes
Replace custom exporter path with an otel-collector gRPC exporter for stability and batching guarantees
Introduce a dynamic metric pruning layer (configurable per-service) to bound metric cardinality
Reduce allocations in trace span handling by enabling zero-copy propagation and pooled buffers
Establish safe rollout plan with canaries and automated rollback criteria tied to latency and telemetry drop metrics
acceptance_criteria: OpenTelemetry SDK upgraded to v1.16.x across runtime and agent packages with no compile-time warnings
Telemetry exporter switched to otel-collector gRPC with batching enabled; exporter failures backpressure upstream rather than dropping silently
Metric cardinality for the targeted service bucket reduced by >= 60% in staging during synthetic traffic
End-to-end telemetry CPU usage on instrumented nodes reduced by >=15% during a 5-minute burst test
No increase in dropped spans or missing attributes in production after canary rollout; baselined using observability-health dashboard
tasks: Audit all services that use the legacy otel shim and list packages requiring API changes
Prototype gRPC exporter config and local otel-collector with batching/timeout policies
Implement dynamic metric pruning wrapper that normalizes labels and caps unique label sets per metric
Add pooled buffer and zero-copy propagation in runtime span creation path
Run load tests comparing old vs new pipeline under bursty RPS and synthetic high-cardinality labels
Prepare PRs, review, and land upgrades with feature flags to toggle collector vs local exporter
Canary rollout to staging, then 10% of production hosts for 48 hours with watchbook playbook
Converge dashboards: telemetry ingestion success rate, exporter queue lengths, runtime p50/p95 latency
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Spike complete. Validated that otel-collector gRPC exporter reduces exporter goroutine stalls in local repro. Prototype config checked in: ops/otel/collector/grpc-batching.yaml (link in related_prs).
2025-02-19: Implemented basic metric pruning wrapper. Early tests show unique label reduction ~40% for the auth-service synthetic suite.
2025-02-24: Replaced the legacy shim in runtime-tracing package with upstream SDK adapter. Required minor API adjustments to context propagation; no behavioral changes in tests.
2025-02-27: Load test (10k RPS burst) shows CPU drop ~18% on telemetry workers and exporter queueing absorbed by collector batching. Preparing PRs for review.
2025-03-02: PRs open: core runtime upgrade + pruning + collector config. Requesting cross-team review from infra and telemetry owners. Starting canary deployment planning.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Collector becomes a single point of failure and could add latency. Mitigation: deploy collector as fault-tolerant pool with local fallback exporter and circuit breaker policy.
Risk: Metric pruning may remove attributes useful for debugging. Mitigation: make pruning config per-service with an allowlist and sample retention for a short window (72h).
Risk: Upgrading SDK surfaces hidden behavior changes. Mitigation: run end-to-end tests against golden traces and compare attribute parity; enable feature flag to revert to old shim quickly.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Merge feature-flagged PRs and deploy to staging cluster. Run synthetic burst tests and validate dashboards.
Stage 2: Canary 10% production hosts for 48 hours. Monitor p50/p95 latency, exporter queue, span drop rate. Hold/rollback if span drop >0.5% or p95 increases >10%.
Stage 3: If canary is clean, expand to 50% then full rollout over 3 days with progressive scaling of collector capacity.
Stage 4: Post-rollback measures documented and retrospective scheduled if any incidents occur.
notes: Design review scheduled with Observability guild on 2025-03-04.
Infra requested extra quota for collector pools in us-west-2 during canary.
Follow-up ticket suggested: global metric naming hygiene pass to avoid future churn (PM to prioritize).
